teams.name: Cachasol Cartel

nameHistory.name: C u M C back KIDZ!!!

teams.commentary: Mike D. once called his team Deja Vu Crew, and the quarterback room remains committed to the bit: Dak Prescott scored nearly 20 on the bench while Jayden Daniels started and scored less, at least the third time this season the Cartel has started the wrong quarterback. It didn't matter, because everything else hit. The Cartel posted the top score of the week, beat all eleven teams in the all-play and handled Sam by 32, with Bhayshul Tuten going for 28.9 out of the flex and the Steelers defense, the other Frum trade arrival, scoring second-best in the league. The one dud was Javonte Williams, the $10 keeper, at about a third of his projection. With Terry McLaurin on IR and Tyreek Hill carrying a questionable tag, the receivers behind Ja'Marr Chase and George Pickens are thin, but the first-place team can afford to shop.

teams.name: Ammonia Coladas
teams.commentary: The Coladas keep doing the boring thing, which is winning by a lot. This week it was Tee Higgins' turn, 32.5 points on a projection of 13, the biggest overperformance in the league, and Mark beat Foy by 44 with Malik Nabers and Nico Collins both on bye, a flex of roster depth most of this league can only envy. The blemishes were at the bottom of the box score: Will Reichard kicked a single point and Chris Godwin Jr. scored a zero in the lineup. Lamar Jackson is now OUT after Buffalo's rout of Baltimore, so Drake Maye is the only healthy quarterback on the roster, and Chris Rodriguez Jr., the fresh pickup, started in the flex while Kenny Gainwell outscored him from the bench. Mark gets Frum next, which is the closest thing this league offers to a bye.

teams.name: DINO NUGGETS

nameHistory.name: The Man the Myth the Legend

teams.commentary: My Chemical Romance just landed its first No. 1 album with a record that came out twenty years ago, and Baker just started the right tight end, which felt like it took about as long. Harold Fannin Jr., the $18 keeper, finally got the nod over Dallas Goedert and scored 18.4, Jahmyr Gibbs and Chuba Hubbard combined for 45, and the Dino Nuggets beat Jordan by more than 40 to climb to third. The Seahawks defense scored a single point, and Jakobi Meyers played through a questionable tag for 3.4, but those are the complaints of a team that won going away. Baker made no moves this week and didn't need to, since Rico Dowdle scored double digits on the bench as the only real back behind Gibbs and Hubbard. The Dino Nuggets get Foy next, and the second-softest remaining schedule in the league after that.

teams.name: $200 Dolla Holla
teams.commentary: Top-ranked Miami had to sweat out North Carolina by three on Saturday; Hearn had to sweat out Jeff by 0.6 on Sunday, and he did it with four players who weren't on his roster a week ago. Every one of them started: the Jaguars defense led the league with 21 a week after the Titans gave him a zero, and Antonio Williams, Evan McPherson and Malik Washington chipped in the rest of the margin and then some. D'Andre Swift, flagged as his worst pick on draft day, went for nearly 27, which makes August look worse every week. Hearn is 4-4, up three spots to fourth, and finally collecting some of the luck his all-play record has been owed all season. The receiver room is still a triage tent, with A.J. Brown, Emeka Egbuka and Deebo Samuel all carrying questionable tags and Alec Pierce on IR, so the waiver wire is doing the work of a trade.

teams.name: Captain Casper's Low Risk Tacos

nameHistory.name: Coach Matty Ps D In Swishs V

teams.commentary: Josh Allen passed Jim Kelly for the most touchdown passes in Bills history on Sunday, and Brett A. got 26.4 out of it, plus 16 from Tyler Bass, a fresh pickup kicking in Buffalo's rout of Baltimore. The Tacos beat Hess by 58 with only the seventh-best score of the week, which the committee files under scheduling and rewards with a three-spot climb anyway. The other pickup, Ryan Flournoy, started and scored double digits, so the waiver work was sharp. The roster churn has a cost, though: Brett dropped RJ Harvey and Dameon Pierce a week after both scored double digits on his bench, and their replacements, J.K. Dobbins and Corey Kiner, combined for about 5. With DeVonta Smith and Mack Hollins on IR and Chris Olave on a Saints bye, the receiver room was Keenan Allen and a waiver claim, and the hardest remaining schedule in the league starts with Danny.

teams.name: Christopher Dootron
teams.commentary: Sam finally ran into somebody who scores points, and the Dootron fell three spots to sixth. Bijan Robinson managed 7.6 on a projection over 18, Parker Washington, the $10 keeper, scored about 3, and Jordan Mason started at running back and contributed 2, so the backfield the committee has worried about all season got healthy and still didn't show up. The pickups were fine: Kyler Murray, Baker's castoff from a few weeks back, started and scored nearly 20, and Chad Ryland became the latest tenant of the kicker slot, outscoring Chris Boswell, the kicker Sam cut, by a point. Michael Wilson scored 22.8 through a questionable tag, which kept this from getting ugly. Sam has the softest remaining schedule in the league, which is the most Sam sentence possible.

teams.name: Papas McButt Nuggets

nameHistory.name: Why dont you just call them?

teams.commentary: Tom Hanks brought David S. Pumpkins back to SNL on Halloween, and Jordan brought back his own recurring bit: an enormous number sitting on his bench. This week it was Tyler Allgeier, 33.6 points in reserve while Jeremiyah Love, flagged as his worst pick on draft day, scored 2.3 in the flex, the bench bomb of the week in a 41-point loss. Jonathan Taylor, the $48 keeper, added under 5, and the Browns defense scored 2. Jordan has now left nearly 184 points on his bench this season, the most in the league by a distance, and he cut Bo Nix to make room for Malik Willis, who scored on the bench while Nix scored 19.2 for Jeff. The silver lining is that Allgeier, Rhamondre Stevenson and Mike Washington Jr. give him running backs to sell, and with Carnell Tate out and Jordyn Tyson on IR, a receiver is exactly what he should be buying.

teams.name: Table Shepherds McPie

nameHistory.name: your son rip  on line toot
Fernet and The Music Hall Mack

teams.commentary: Foy needed a kicker and a receiver this week and ended up with neither. The Table Shepherds scored 79.2, lost to Mark by 44 and slid two spots, with DK Metcalf contributing 0.9 and Jared Goff 9, which isn't a passing attack so much as a passing suggestion. Ladd McConkey, the $18 keeper, scored double digits on the bench, and Blake Corum outscored Makai Lemon, the new pickup in the flex. The kicker saga has reached its final act: Tyler Loop kicked 2 and is now on IR, and there is no other kicker on the roster, which for once is a genuine gap rather than a joke. Jonah Coleman, flagged as his worst pick on draft day, scored 18.4, and with Corum and Dylan Sampson also behind Kyren Williams, the backfield is suddenly the deepest part of this roster, so Foy has a back to sell for the receiver he obviously needs.

teams.name: Quintosss... Amigo?
teams.commentary: Patrick Mahomes threw three touchdowns in Denver and then got sacked on the final play of a four-point loss, and Jeff's Sunday followed the same script. The Amigos posted the third-best score of the week, with Tony Pollard, Brock Bowers and Mahomes all booming, and lost to Hearn by 0.6 because Rashee Rice scored 14.8 on the bench while Drake London scored 1.3 in the lineup. Khalil Shakir and Brian Thomas Jr. would each have flipped it too, which makes this the most self-inflicted loss of the week. Jeff did make one sharp move, grabbing Bo Nix off Jordan's scrap heap and correctly keeping him behind Mahomes, and he swapped the Ravens defense for the Cowboys, which was right by four points. With Tyjae Spears out and Tank Bigsby on IR, Pollard is the only real back behind Quinshon Judkins and Braelon Allen, and four spare receivers make Jeff an obvious buyer.

teams.name: Los Desperados Sudados
teams.commentary: Joe Burrow threw for 462 yards in an overtime shootout with the Titans, and Danny got 39.4 fantasy points of it, the best day by any quarterback in the league and his best draft-day value playing like it. Los Desperados beat Frum by 68, the second-biggest margin of the season, and for once the bench didn't decide anything. It was still loaded: Dalton Kincaid, DeMario Douglas and DJ Moore all scored double digits in reserve, while the Broncos defense started and scored 1, the worst in the league. Chase McLaughlin, the new kicker, scored 12, so the Zvada experiment is over. Danny is 2-6 with the worst luck number in the league, and with Travis Etienne and Isiah Pacheco on IR, Rachaad White and Bam Knight are the backfield depth, so one of those spare receivers should become a running back by Friday.

teams.name: For Heaven Sakes, Woman
teams.commentary: Hess started the Bengals defense in a 43-36 overtime track meet and got 2, while the Rams scored 11 on his bench, a choice a coin flip would have gotten right half the time. For Heaven Sakes, Woman scored 59.3, the third-lowest total of the season, and lost to the Tacos by 58. Matthew Stafford, flagged as his worst pick on draft day, managed 8.2 through a questionable tag, Tre Tucker scored a zero in the flex, and Isaiah Davis, a fresh pickup, started at running back and scored 1.5. Christian McCaffrey was on bye, which explains some of it, and Puka Nacua was the only starter who seemed aware there was a game. With Jonathon Brooks on IR and TreVeyon Henderson questionable, the backs behind McCaffrey are this week's pickups, and outside of KC Concepcion there isn't much on this roster anybody would trade for.

teams.name: Dad Bellies Doin' Salt Smellies

Poopy Wake Up Call On Line Toot
The Best Butt of the Bunch

teams.commentary: Frum once named his team Wilson!?!? WILSON IM SORRY, and this week the apology went the other way: Michael Wilson, flagged as Frum's best value on draft day and now on Sam's roster, scored 22.8, while Frum's entire lineup scored 59.2, the second-lowest total of the season. Zay Flowers, the $21 keeper, scored a zero, Spencer Shrader kicked 1, and Emmett Johnson scored as much as Wilson did, on Frum's bench, while Denzel Boston started in the flex. The Commanders defense, a fresh pickup, scored 14, third-best in the league, which is a genuinely good move buried in a 68-point loss. Alvin Kamara and Cam Skattebo were both on bye, so the trade haul gave him nothing again. Frum is 1-7 with Mark up next and more running backs than receivers, so anyone with a spare wideout should be calling.

commentary.intro: Milwaukee ended a 57-year wait for a World Series title on Wednesday, which gives hope to every long-suffering franchise except, apparently, Frum's. The Bellies posted 59.2, the second-lowest score of the season, lost to all eleven teams in the all-play and fell to 1-7. At the other end, Mike D.'s Cartel ran the table with the week's top score, and the Frum trade keeps paying out, with Bhayshul Tuten and the Steelers defense combining for nearly 45. Mark and Baker won easily and hold second and third, while Sam, Jordan and Foy all lost and slid. The climbers are Hearn and Brett A., up three spots apiece: Hearn by winning a 0.6-point thriller with four brand-new players in his lineup, Brett by drawing Hess. And then there's Jordan, who left a 33-point running back on his bench, and we will be discussing that at some length.

awards.benchBomb: Jordan benched Tyler Allgeier's 33.6 for Jeremiyah Love's 2.3, a 31-point swing, and Love, flagged as his worst pick on draft day, did exactly what August said he would.
awards.closest: Hearn over Jeff by 0.6, and Jeff wrote his own ending: Rashee Rice, Khalil Shakir and Brian Thomas Jr. each would have flipped it from the bench while Drake London scored 1.3 in the lineup.
awards.lowScore: Frum scored 59.2, the second-lowest total of the season, lost to all eleven teams in the all-play, and got a zero from his $21 keeper Zay Flowers.
awards.highScore: Cachasol Cartel, 131.4, a perfect 11-0 all-play week with the Frum trade's leftovers doing the heavy lifting.
awards.blowout: Danny over Frum by 68.1, the second-biggest margin of the season, and Danny did it with three double-digit receivers on his bench.
awards.bestDefense: Hearn picked up the Jaguars a week after the Titans gave him a zero, started them, and got 21, the best defensive score in the league.
awards.worstDefense: Danny's Broncos, projected 11th of 12, scored 1, which is roughly what the draft-day grade predicted.
awards.boom: Tee Higgins, projected 13, scored 32.5 for Mark.
awards.bust: Zay Flowers, projected 16.7, scored zero for Frum.
awards.luckiestWin: Brett A. won by 58 with the seventh-best score of the week. Scheduling is a skill.
awards.toughestLoss: Jeff scored 127.6, third-best in the league, and lost by 0.6.
awards.questionableStart: Foy started Makai Lemon over Blake Corum, and Corum outscored him from the bench.

commentary.outro:
Week 9 headliner: Mike D. against Hearn, first against fourth, the hottest team in the league against the manager whose waiver claims just won him a game by 0.6. Sam and Jordan meet in a sixth-versus-seventh game between two 5-3 teams that both just lost, and one of them gets to stop sliding. Baker gets Foy, who needs a kicker by Sunday, Brett A. gets Danny in a meeting of the reigning champ and the league's unluckiest team, Jeff gets Hess, and Mark gets Frum.

Trade Desk: running backs are still the currency, but this week the banks are easy to spot. Jordan has Tyler Allgeier, Rhamondre Stevenson and Mike Washington Jr. and nobody healthy at receiver behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Garrett Wilson; Jeff has Rashee Rice, Khalil Shakir and Brian Thomas Jr. and nothing behind Pollard. Allgeier for Rice fixes both rosters on the spot. Danny is the other natural seller, with DeMario Douglas, DJ Moore and Rome Odunze all idle at receiver and two backs on IR; Frum has backs he can't use, so Douglas for Emmett Johnson is the cleanest fit on the board. Brett A. needs a receiver more than anyone in the top half and should be calling Danny before they play. Foy has Corum and Sampson to sell and a receiver hole to fill. Move of the week: Hearn dropping the Titans defense after its zero, picking up the Jaguars, starting them and getting 21 in a game he won by 0.6. Anti-move of the week: Jordan cutting Bo Nix for Malik Willis and watching Nix score 19.2 for Jeff.

Keeper Corner: eight weeks in, exactly one keeper in the league is beating the league average of about 15 points per dollar, and it's Mark's Drake Maye, 160 points on $10. Mike D.'s Javonte Williams and Jordan's Jaxon Smith-Njigba are the next-best bargains, both comfortably over 10 per dollar. The big tickets are earning their points slowly: Jahmyr Gibbs at $71 has nearly 179 points, about 2.5 per dollar, and James Cook at $49 sits around 126. The basement still belongs to Hearn's Alec Pierce, $10 for under 10 points and on IR, with Foy's $18 Ladd McConkey on the bench and under 45 points. Zay Flowers, Frum's $21 keeper, scored a zero this week, which did not help the average. Sam's other keeper is long gone and Hess kept nobody at all, which at this point counts as a philosophy. Rankings and commentary refresh every Tuesday morning once ESPN finalizes the week.
